## v1.3.2

### Settings, rebuilt as a document

- The settings screen now reads as a single document with a summary rail: the chapters (GitHub access, current state, preferences, repository control) navigate on click, and the active one follows the scroll. On narrow screens the rail becomes a horizontal strip.
- Every group of rows lives on its own surface, with one type scale for the whole page — chapter titles, group labels and rows no longer compete.
- The repository controls (search, filters, sort and the group accordions) were brought to the same scale, and the group actions became real buttons.

### The token tells you what it can do

- Connecting a token now reports its kind (classic or fine-grained) and probes the four read permissions the app needs — repository metadata, contents, actions and Dependabot alerts — marking each as granted, missing or not verified.
- Before pasting, the screen lists the permissions a token needs and links straight to GitHub's creation pages for fine-grained and classic tokens.
- The old diagnostics card is gone: each fact now appears once, in the chapter it belongs to.

### Preferences in a row each

- Theme, language and detail level are one row per setting: label on the left, control on the right.
- The theme dropdown carries the color dot inside the control — in the closed state and in every option.
- The detail level hint follows the active level instead of always describing the balanced one.

### A settings screen with its own chrome

- On the settings route the top bar drops its search, refresh and settings shortcuts and keeps a single back-home control: the settings themselves already live on the screen.
- The page closes with a footer showing the app version and a link to the repository, which always opens outside the app — a new tab in the browser, the system browser on the desktop build.

## v1.3.1

### Maintenance patch

This is a maintenance release: no intended change to how the app looks or behaves.

- Styling stack upgraded to Tailwind CSS 4. Theme tokens, the custom type scale and the dialog/accordion animations were preserved and verified against the generated stylesheet.
- Dependency updates across the app and its tooling (Radix radio group, the Tauri store and window-state plugins, ESLint, Testing Library's jest-dom). `npm audit` is clean again: the advisory chain without an upstream fix that had been blocking every pull request is gone.
- The desktop development server now names its port (5300) and checks the loopback before starting, so a dev window cannot attach to another project's server by accident.

## v1.3.0

### Private repositories, where they belong

- The desktop app and the local secure mode can now discover and track **private** repositories once you connect a GitHub token.
- The published GitHub Pages site is unchanged on purpose: it never lists, reads or publishes a private repository.
- Private repositories are opt-in. "Select public" never turns them on, and you add them on purpose from their own group.

### Knowing what your token can see

- The token panel now reports two numbers: how many repositories are in scope for your token, and how many of them are private.
- If a fine-grained token does not reach your private repositories, the panel explains how to grant it, instead of silently showing an empty list.

### Repository control, organized

- The repository list is grouped and shown in the order Public, Private, Others, Forks.
- A repository lands in exactly one group: a fork whose upstream is out of your token goes to Forks, then private, then archived, then public.
- Each group has its own select and clear actions, its own counter, can be collapsed, and keeps its header in place while you scroll through a long list.
- The search and the All / Selected / Unselected filters work inside every group, and a group never disappears because a filter hid its items.

### A list you can size

- The repository list is resizable: drag the divider on its right edge and the width follows the pointer.
- Drag it all the way in and the list collapses into the icon rail; drag it back out and it expands to the width you had.
- The width is remembered between sessions, the divider works from the keyboard (arrow keys, Home and End) and double-clicking it toggles the rail.

### Forks that say where they come from

- A fork is no longer just a repository: push_ resolves its upstream and shows "Fork of owner/repository" when the upstream is accessible.
- When the upstream is outside your token, the row says so, and the fork gets its own group.

### Nothing private is stored or published

- The local cache was rebuilt so that no private repository data is ever written to disk: only public names can appear, and everything else is rebuilt from the token at runtime.
- Snapshot generation refuses to publish a private repository, even if it is listed in the tracking config.
- The privacy invariant is now enforced by tests on both the cache and the publishing path.
